prompt: Match each selector to what it reaches. There are options left over in the right-hand column.
hint: Two of them differ by a single character between the names, and that difference is the distance in the tree.

pairs.right: Every link at any depth inside nav
Only the links that are direct children of nav
Each item that comes right after another item
Links whose address starts with http

right_distractors: The first item of every list on the page
Links inside an element with the class http

prompt: Two rules reach the same element: `#panel p { color: red }` and `.warning.featured p { color: blue }`. Which colour wins, and why?
hint: Specificity is a trio compared from left to right. How many classes would it take to beat an id?

choices.text: Red: the id counts in the first number of the trio, and that is compared before the classes — no number of classes reaches it.
choices.why: (1,0,1) against (0,2,1): the first number decides and the others are never even consulted.

choices.text: Blue: two classes add up to more weight than one id, because the sum is a weighted total.
choices.why: The sum is not a total: it is a position-by-position comparison, and the first difference settles it.

choices.text: Blue: between rules reaching the same element, the one written last always wins.
choices.why: Order only breaks a tie when specificity ties, which is not the case here.

choices.text: Red: `color` is inherited, and inherited properties ignore specificity.
choices.why: Inheritance explains how a child gets a value with no rule of its own; here there are two direct rules, and the cascade decides.
